questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The traditions of the University towards my special interest in my field, i.e. Ancient History in University of Edinburgh.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The flow of information was sometimes inadequate and confusing, especially when not all things apply to all universities/exchanges.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Slightly hard. It was easy for me, because the process in UK is much more straightforward than e.g. Italy etc. It was confusing not to know how much applied to my exchange or what was in general. I also feel like I was left be to find out most of the stuff on my own.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a intro week with tutors etc. Many intro days and other events for newcomers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard, and since it was implied that student accommodation was hard to aquire, I felt like i had no chioce really. The housing options for students was in very poor quality for me to even consider University accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: be on the look in good time, and take what you can get...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I heard from the other students in uni accommodation had problems with molds, mice, and broken utilities etc. that the responsible personnel did not have time to fix. Also, the alternative options for housing were sparse and very, very expensive!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: it was easy to apply, but i felt the criteria for getting the courses was weirdly bureaucratic. For example, I wanted courses in Ancient History but couldn't because I only have had courses in History (even though many of the courses were de facto about ancient history). There was also unnecessary language requirements, to my opinion.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: fine, straightforward. Could be worse I guess.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: relatively little. can't think of any

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: unsuccessful. got my alternative priorities, but not at all any of the courses i wanted, and specifically applied for the university to learn. very disappointing .

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the lecturers were awful, and the 'tutorials' were weird, awkward and unnecessary. The Lectures were very poorly structured, sometime more of a 'I wanna talk about what I want and not about the exam' - overall poorly structures according to the exams.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: easy, but poorly structured

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it was far worse than at CPH! I am glad to be home. Very unpersonal...

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Connections since 1450
English Discovery of Russia, 1556-1664
Themes in Modern European History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not the ones I had!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were clubs for everything (incl. Garlic appreciation which I found a bit weird)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All the kinds I imagine.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Idk

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Sightseeing, it depends of the city of course!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A bit hard. I loathe the british food culture (ew), but the overall city was easy to get around. Luckily Edinburgh is as much digitalised as CPH! People were very kind:-)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, attend stuff, be open!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The food!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness towards others, and kindness towards strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get out of the city some days (e.g. the highlands)
Explore! walk around, also in the not-so-touristed places
Get a alternative accommodation outside the city centre, (e.g. Portobello where I lived), to get a glimpse of the suburban areas and stuff tourists do not see.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Generally being in a foreign country, forced to speak English. Adapting on their (and my new) lifestyle. You'll learn a lot from that.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from everyone and everything. Being in a strange country where you know no people, and have no knowledge of the foods, supermarkets, stores, rules etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
